items.title: Power torsion modules become invariant under base change exactly when the quotients by the ideal agree
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a pair satisfying the equivalent conditions of the preceding characterization of flatness on torsion, the natural map from every power torsion module to its base change is an isomorphism exactly when the quotient of the base by the ideal is isomorphic to the corresponding quotient of the target (statement lines 24263-24273). The proof is a two-stage induction: the case of a module annihilated by the ideal is a direct computation over the quotient, and the general case of a module annihilated by a fixed power is handled by the displayed short exact sequence with flatness carrying the hypothesis on the outer terms to the middle, after which an arbitrary power torsion module is treated as the union of these and the conclusion follows from commutation of tensor products with colimits (proof lines 24275-24297). The induction with the outer terms is what makes the statement sharp. The counted statement depends on the preceding characterization, which is delivered as a context span so that its label resolves inside the package, and there is no further reference, so the card carries no navigation stub.
